blocks.md: **Commuting zones more exposed to rising Chinese imports saw larger falls in manufacturing employment, more unemployment and non-participation, more disability receipt and lower wages — with no offsetting migration. Moving from the 25th to the 75th percentile of exposure growth (a 1.06 difference in $1,000 of imports per worker) implies a 4.5% larger fall in manufacturing employment and a 0.8% larger fall in weekly earnings.**

blocks.title: Lecture caveat
blocks.md: These are the paper's own results. The lecture notes that they are now considered problematic and leaves the critique to the first assignment — see [Shift-Share Instrument](note:shift-share-instrument) for the issues commonly raised.

Design: change in imports from China per worker, built from regional industry employment shares ([Shift-Share Exposure](note:shift-share-exposure)), instrumented with other high-income countries' imports from China and lagged shares. 722 CZs × two periods (1990–2000, 2000–2007), ten-year-equivalent changes, controls for the start-of-period manufacturing share and other regional characteristics, standard errors clustered by state.

blocks.md:
| Ten-year change in average log weekly wage (log pts) | All | Males | Females |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All education levels | −0.759*** | −0.892*** | −0.614*** |
| College | −0.757** | −0.991*** | −0.525* |
| No college | −0.814*** | −0.703*** | −1.116*** |
The difference in exposure growth is 1.06. Multiplying:

| Outcome | Calculation | Differential |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manufacturing employees | 1.06 × (−4.231) | −4.5% |
| Manufacturing emp/pop | 1.06 × (−0.596) | −0.63 pp |
| Employment/pop | 1.06 × (−0.596 − 0.178) | −0.82 pp |
| Number unemployed | 1.06 × 4.921 | +5.2% |
| Unemployed/pop | 1.06 × 0.221 | +0.23 pp |
| Mean weekly earnings | 1.06 × (−0.759) | −0.8% |

- **Relative, not aggregate**: effects compare more- to less-exposed regions; anything common to all regions is absorbed.
- **Non-college workers lose outside manufacturing too** (non-manufacturing employment −0.531 pp) and leave the labor force (+0.831 pp): local spillovers.
- **No migration response** means the losses stay local — consistent with a regional, immobile-factor view.
